newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan jets bomb palace in rebel-held Jalalabad.
newsitem.headline: Afghan jets bomb palace in rebel-held Jalalabad.

text.p: Two Afghan government jets bombed a former royal palace in the rebel-held eastern city of Jalalabad on Sunday, an Afghan news agency reported.

The Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press said the raid, at 9.15 a.m. (0445 GMT), had damaged the building, which had been used by former provincial governor Haji Abdul Qadir until the Islamic Taleban militia captured the city on Wednesday.
There was no immediate word on casualties.

The Taleban, fighting to oust President Burhanuddin Rabbani and install a strict Islamic order in Afghanistan, seized Jalalabad, on the main Kabul-Pakistan highway, in a lightning advance through eastern provinces last week.

Afghan sources in Pakistan said on Saturday that government forces had checked the Taleban advance towards the strategic town of Sarobi, about 60 km (37 miles) east of Kabul, and the border province of Kunar, northeast of Jalalabad.
Jalalabad, capital of Nangarhar province, had been held by a group of neutral factions led by Haji Qadir that had stayed out of fighting between rival guerrilla groups since April 1992.
